dataFlow.name: Opt-in durable county ingestion
steps: With FIREAFTER_DURABLE_REFRESH_ENABLED=true, authorized incident/refresh requests require a durable operation UUID and return HTTP 202 after enqueue, not after a county-wide refresh.
Supabase holds actor/org-scoped job state. Vercel Workflow invokes leased steps using only the opaque job UUID. Private checkpoints remain server-owned.
Core sources publish an initial bundle for a new county; existing refreshes keep the previous committed inventory visible. Extended providers and 128-asset terrain chunks checkpoint independently.

Hydrography acquisition enumerates matching IDs, saves bounded batches and re-verifies the whole set in separate leased steps. Mutable cursor/budget state replaces atomically; original retrieval times and aggregate byte reservations survive resumption. Saved counts alone never publish a partial source.

Bounded transfer chunks are assembled inside Postgres; the existing bundle fence and a phase receipt commit atomically. Replay reconciles receipt identity and never silently rebases over changed evidence.

UI preserves the original reference, polls actor-scoped progress and links to committed evidence. A daily secret-authenticated sweep recovers missed dispatches; normal continuation uses Workflow, not browser polling or cron.
Local SQL and public-provider evidence do not prove hosted Workflow, PostGIS persistence, browser or operational capacity acceptance. Production remains opt-in pending rollout approval.

dataFlow.name: Judge product feature graph and public code graph
steps: The static /features route renders the typed eleven-feature catalog without authentication, incident reads, or live API calls.
Feature nodes expose their documented screens, API interfaces, evidence sources, real test files, and limits; selecting a node updates the detail panel by pointer or keyboard.
The dashboard and feature detail panel link to /features and /code-graph.html respectively; the feature guide documents both public entry points.

publish:code-graph validates the dated Graphify report and the installed vis-network 9.1.6 bundle integrity before generating public/code-graph.html and public/vendor/vis-network.min.js with a snapshot disclosure and return link.

The public viewer loads its integrity-pinned same-origin vendor bundle for reliable rendering; generated graph artifacts remain excluded from future Graphify scans, while the dated snapshot is intentionally included in Vercel public assets.

steps: Route page calls getClientDashboardBundle.
fireafter-data tries Supabase bundle.
fireafter-supabase filters known legacy smoke/demo source evidence and operational records row by row while preserving real source-backed assets, recommendations, and responder decisions.
If no persisted incident exists, fireafter-data returns an honest empty dashboard shell with no sources, assets, or recommendations.
Fixture data is available only in tests or when FIREAFTER_ENABLE_FIXTURES=true.
fireafter-data redacts critical-facility names, precise coordinates, source ids, responder notes, and audit snapshots before returning public/viewer bundles.
fireafter-data compacts heavy source rawPayload arrays before serializing the bundle into Client Component props; full geometry remains server-side for /api/map/features.
FireAfterDashboard renders incident, sources, recommendations, assets, actions, and audit events from the returned bundle.

dataFlow.name: County search and incident creation
steps: Dashboard calls GET /api/search with query.
search route calls searchLocationsLive.
searchLocationsLive queries Census/TIGERweb and returns only real county matches.
Dashboard posts selected locationId to POST /api/incident.
POST /api/incident requires Supabase Auth membership, creates an incident, runs live refresh, and persists to Supabase.

dataFlow.name: Live refresh and scoring
steps: Dashboard or cron calls refresh endpoint.
Manual refresh requires Supabase Auth membership; cron fails closed unless CRON_SECRET is configured and matched by the bearer token.

Cron discovers never-refreshed and least-recently-refreshed persisted incidents from Supabase, hard-caps each run at 20 even if FIREAFTER_CRON_INCIDENT_LIMIT is higher, returns client-safe per-incident status, and fails the HTTP request when any incident fails instead of hiding a partial run or using a hard-coded demo incident.
refreshIncidentBundle loads persisted Supabase incident/assets when available.

runLiveSourceRefresh runs NWS forecast/alerts/observations, WFIGS current/YTD, FIRMS, MTBS, PWFDF, TIGERweb roads, USGS 3DHP, EPQS, FHWA/BTS NBI bridges, and TNM Structures adapters; county-wide 3DEP batch failure is recorded as delayed/partial terrain coverage with unknown per-asset slope and reduced confidence, while malformed samples and local/root deadline or cancellation fail closed.

live-sources converts real results into source snapshots, source-backed bridge/facility assets, inferred/uploaded assets, derived signals, and recommendations; ArcGIS JSON errors become source failures instead of empty online coverage.
source-coverage maps every planned source category to Live, Partial / Proxy, Upload Required, Delayed, or Not Available for API and UI display.
scoring calculates weighted priority score and risk band.
Manual incident, refresh, and asset-import responses return client-safe bundles with compact source rawPayload summaries instead of raw road/hydro/facility feature arrays.
Dashboard displays the six-question recommendation clarity checklist, source evidence, limitations, and freshness so ranked actions stay explainable rather than predictive.
fireafter-data persists refreshed bundle to Supabase or returns explicit error when production persistence fails.

dataFlow.name: Responder action and audit
steps: Dashboard POSTs action payload without trusted actor fields; Modify uses an explicit priority selector and required note instead of a hard-coded priority.
POST /api/actions requires Supabase Auth membership and stamps actor id/email server-side.
audit helpers create immutable recommendation snapshot and audit event.

fireafter-supabase sends each authenticated decision and actor-stamped audit event to one service-role-only command RPC. The original actor/command receipt replays unchanged; different content under that identity rejects. Action, audit and receipt commit together or roll back together.
Dashboard shows action confirmation linking to History & Audit.

Incident-qualified History links open private retained metadata pagination for authorized commanders/analysts and a redacted recent preview for public/viewer sessions. Private history retrieves original evidence separately, preserving nullable actor IDs and provenance flags without synthetic audit, current inventory membership filtering or stored-history rewrites. Failed reads are explicit; evidence above 8 MiB still requires operator export. Real SQL, hosted identity and complete reconciliation acceptance remain open.

dataFlow.name: Asset import
steps: Dashboard blocks read-only sessions before import, then POSTs JSON text or multipart file upload to /api/assets/import for signed-in responders.
Import route requires Supabase Auth membership.
fireafter-store parses CSV or GeoJSON FeatureCollection against the active incident context, skips invalid rows/features, and adds audit event with import errors.
fireafter-data persists imported assets and audit event to Supabase for an existing incident, refreshes live sources/recommendations, or errors rather than inventing a fallback incident.

Dashboard applies the returned compact bundle so Assets, source snapshots, recommendations, and History stay synchronized, while keeping validation errors visible and preserving the pasted content when no asset imported.
Assets view labels inferred crossings as source-backed candidates from public roads/hydrography and positions local uploads as the high-confidence validation path.

dataFlow.name: Operational health
steps: Settings view calls GET /api/readiness for the current incident.
readiness route loads the current dashboard bundle and probes Supabase reality-upgrade schema readiness.

readiness service maps source, auth, audit, and workflow checks to transparent operational, needs-attention, or blocked categories; reachable no-coverage and refreshed fallback-age source results are treated as visible evidence rather than retry work, public read-only readiness does not penalize already-proven role-gated write workflows, Responder Workflow only passes when an accept/modify action has matching audit evidence, and deployment remains blocked until both server-owned-write and atomic responder-action live control versions are verified.

product-promise audit checks integrated source coverage, map/layer evidence, basin-to-asset linkage, complete ranked-item clarity, responsible decision-support language, and audit-preserved source/user context.
SystemHealthPanel shows scores, blockers, deployment actions, and the operator checklist; ProductPromisePanel shows pass/gap states and next actions.
Settings copy frames stale, delayed, or missing feeds as honest degraded mode rather than hidden replacement data.
